headline: Approved water rate increases, property sales, event permits, and ordinance changes; postponed Eco Hospitality letter of intent 4-3.
summary: The Council heard public comment on youth gun violence and public safety, then approved traffic schedule changes, several property dispositions, a water rate increase, multiple outdoor event permits, and first or final passage of several ordinance amendments. It also approved a credit enhancement agreement for Martel School Apartments Phase III and voted 4-3 to postpone the Eco Hospitality Consultants letter of intent for more review.
decisions: Approved an amendment to the Traffic Schedule creating Sections 55 and 56 for parking prohibitions on trash collection days, 7-0.
Approved removing two police-only parking spots at 292 Bates Street from the Traffic Schedule, 7-0.
Approved a municipal quitclaim deed releasing the City's interest in 38 Larrabee Road, 7-0.
Approved the disposition of 71 Brigham Street to Doreen and Joseph Valecko and Adam Rivard for $4,000, 7-0.
Approved the disposition of 1 Carver Street to Doreen and Joseph Valecko and Adam Rivard for $4,000, 7-0.
Approved the disposition of 9 Ceres Avenue to Aron Epps for $500, 7-0.
Appointed Brian O'Malley and Walter Shostak to the Lewiston-Auburn Transit Committee for three-year terms, 7-0.
Approved accepting transfer of forfeiture funds from several court cases into the Drug Enforcement Program account, 7-0.
Accepted the City Clerk's report on verified signatures for the petition to amend the Syringe Service Program ordinance, 7-0.
Voted to send the Syringe Service Program ordinance amendments to a citizen referendum on the November 2026 ballot, 7-0.
Approved amendments to Policy Manual 69 raising water rates, effective August 17, 26, 7-0.
Granted an Outdoor Entertainment Permit for the L/A Balloon Festival at Simard-Payne Park on August 14-21, 7-0.
Granted an Outdoor Entertainment Permit for the Fiddlers' Rendezvous at Kennedy Park on August 9, 7-0.
Granted an Outdoor Entertainment Permit for the Arise Lewiston event at Kennedy Park on July 18, 7-0.
Granted an Outdoor Entertainment Permit for the Outreach in the Park event at Kennedy Park on July 25 and August 22, 7-0.
Gave final passage to an amendment adding access times for the South Lewiston Little League Field, 7-0.
Gave first passage to creating Chapter 23 'Residential Rental Properties' and continued the public hearing to the next meeting, 7-0.
Gave first passage to removing the Rental Registration section from Chapter 18 and continued the public hearing, 7-0.
Gave first passage to removing the public hearing requirement for Outdoor Entertainment Permits and continued the public hearing, 7-0.
Gave first passage to removing the list of city parks from the Business License ordinance and continued the public hearing, 7-0.
Gave first passage to changes for the No Name Pond Conservation Overlay District and continued the public hearing, 7-0.
Adopted an order authorizing the City Administrator to execute a credit enhancement agreement for Martel School Apartments Phase III, 7-0.
Voted 4-3 to postpone the Letter of Intent with Eco Hospitality Consultants to allow more time to address Council concerns.
Council reached consensus to direct city staff to develop recommendations addressing concerns about social service event permits in city parks.

CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 7, 2026 
 
REGULAR MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 7:00 P.M. 
 
CITY COUNCIL PRESIDENT CHITTIM, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Councilors Nagine, Longchamps, Harriman, Roy, Noble, Chittim, and Martel, City 
Administrator Bryan Kaenrath, Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley, and City Clerk 
Kathleen Montejo. Absent/Excused: Mayor Sheline 
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
VOTE (236-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Harriman: 
 
To enter into an Executive Session pursuant to MRSA Title 1, section 405(6) (A) and (E) to discuss 
a legal matter with the City Attorney.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
Executive Session began at 6:40pm and ended at 7:00 pm. 
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
VOTE (237-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
  
To dispense with the reading of the minutes of the meetings of June 2 and 16, 2026, and to 
accept and place them on file as prepared by the City Clerk.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
Eryn Soule, Ward 5 – Thank you to Councilors of Wards 2 and 7 for demanding public safety 
and follow up. People who live in Ward 5 want safety first as well. Bret Martel, Ward 7 – 
Submitted an agenda item for the meeting agenda but it was blocked and not added. The Council 
previously declared that an anti-ICE ordinance was an emergency but refused to determine this 
agenda item addressing youth gun violence is one. The Mayor has no desire to act. ICE is in 
town based upon Facebook posts. Mayor and Councilor of Ward 3 want businesses to start 
yelling at law enforcement. The Council held a meeting on safety but did not take any action to 
follow up. LPD does a great job, but the Council needs to focus on prevention.  Marcel Leclair, 
Ward 5 – Disappointed with leadership of Mayor and Council. Ward 2 and 7 begged to bring in 
National Guard. Ward 5 Councilor said residents don’t want outside help, but they do, and it is 
needed.  Amy Smit, Ward 3 – Member of the Planning Board.  Thanked the Council for their 
service, know a lot work hard to review material. Council needs to reach out to committee 
members for help.  Ronnie Paradi s, Ward 6 – Why isn’t the Public Health Committee coming to 
the Council to advise them on various matters? Council needs to reach out to the city committees 
and ask for their advice, use the volunteers to do the work. Seniors Plus should help seniors get 
transportation. Melissa Dunn, Blake St. – Last Tuesday’s meeting was a dangerous call to have
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 7, 2026 
                             
2 
 
the National Guard patrol the streets of our community. White supremacists and white 
nationalists will target community members. The comments were racist and inflammatory; 
threats of federal violence. 
 
VOTE (238-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Longchamps, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To suspend the Council Rules and extend public comment beyond the 18-minute limit as set by 
the Rules.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
Nathan Pearl, Lewiston – Need to analyze corruption and fraud. There are 800,000 unhoused 
residents in the United States. Panhandling is increasing. Build skyscrapers, not missiles. Siri 
Cressey, Ward 5 – At least one Councilor called for the National Guard for control in Lewiston.  
That would be catastrophic, calling upon soldiers to go after children. Remember the Kent State 
massacre.  There must be a better way. Martin Chartrand, Ward 3 – It is sad about the gun 
violence in youth. Move to a non-violent approach and repair the situation, not add more harm. 
Media has sensationalized the issue. Black youth are charged at disproportionate rates using the 
“school to prison” pipeline in underfunded schools. Youth compare video games to real life to 
seek attention and approval.  Actions are dehumanizing black youth.  Lisa Jones, Ward 2 – 
Thank goodness for Flock cameras, PD said solving crimes. Been one week since pointless 4-
hour meeting that ended with no action, Council must not want to do anything to solve issue of 
youth gun violence. Mayor is tone-deaf, made a post about fascism over July 4th weekend. 
Mayor wants to wait until after election to do anything. Andrew Jones, Ward 2 – There is a 
sidebar conversation between Harriman and Chittim – be transparent and tell everyone what you 
are talking about. Councilor Martel was right, the Council previously said the anti-ICE ordinance 
was an emergency but they refused to call his agenda item an emergency, but it was enough of 
an emergency last week when the Council held an “emergency” meeting to hear speakers on the 
topic. Councilor Harriman, as a member of the Legislature, could have pledged to bring this 
issue to Augusta to get help but he did not say a word. Ifraax Saciid-Ciise, Ward 2 – Lewiston is 
the youngest city in Maine with the most youth. People are not supporting youth. Summer school 
is kicking kids out. Need to build relationships with youth. Can school stop kicking kids out into 
the streets? The city has been dealing with gun violence for a long time, same issue every 
summer but the media wants to make a big deal about it this year. Need to stop blaming youth 
but invest in them. Robert Glaspy, Ward 6 – Gets more and more frustrated with every meeting 
he attends. Encourage those who have ability to solve them to keep going. Things are so divided, 
so polarized. No solution comes from finger-pointing. Please continue to do work. Matt Agren, 
Ward 4 – We are one Lewiston, but a culture of violence, 13-year-olds and 14-year-olds are 
carrying guns and shooting at each other. This is nationwide and not just Lewiston. Ward 2 
Councilor said her mother is afraid to leave her home because she might get shot. Where are the 
guns coming from, local or away? 
 
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT 
 
The Cart to Curb program will launch soon and more public information sessions are scheduled. 
The Library has started a new program with Woodlands Memory Care proving monthly book 
deliveries to aim to improve quality of life.  If successful, will expand. Trees are being planted 
in the tree streets. The Beyond the Badge event will happen on July 23, everyone is welcome to
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 7, 2026 
                             
3 
 
attend to meet police officers, firefighters, EMTs from United Ambulance and Life Flight.  
Seniors Plus received a $30,000 grant to build a computer lab to benefit older residents. The 
Maine MILL Museum held its grand opening last week.

Acting Director of Development John Blais and Lewiston Housing Authority Director of

VOTE (260-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Harriman, seconded by Councilor Nagine:

Agreement for Martel School Apartments Phase III: 
 
Whereas, Lewiston Housing Authority has permitted 88 units in the first two phases and plans for  
44 more units in phase three containing affordable senior housing at the Former Martel School  
site; and 
 
Whereas, the City Council desires to support development of new housing in Lewiston of a variety  
of configurations, family size, and income levels, and particularly affordable housing for seniors;  
and 
 
Whereas, the development sited at 860-880 Lisbon Street on approximately 3.21 acres of land is  
anticipated to include three phases of 44 units each, with an anticipated combined future assessed

development costs;

Administrator is authorized to execute and negotiate the proposed Phase III credit enhancement  
agreement for Martel School Apartments for general term of (22 Years at 75%).

DISCUSSION REGARDING INCLUSION OF EVENTS PERMITS FOR SOCIAL 
SERVICE PROGRAMMING ON CITY PROPERTIES AND PARKS 
 
Councilor Nagine expressed concerns with organized groups holding outreach events in city 
parks without advanced approval from the city, citing concerns with litter left over after events 
and other related concerns about the use and conditions of the parks after the groups leave. Since 
these groups do not book use of the parks in advance, the city does not know who to hold 
responsible for the trash and other issues. The consensus from the Council was to agree to direct 
city staff to develop recommendations to implement to address the concerns of Councilor Nagine
